A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ParPIC research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E are readable and support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original clustering experiments on K-NN graphs, synthetic DiSBMs, and real directed networks, including AMI results, runtime measurements, and appendix sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains the original clustering experiments and appendix analyses, and reports revised entropy-estimation results and expanded runtime measurements.

M1.justification: Equation 9 corrects the stated entropy-probe computation from left-multiplying a delta column to right-multiplying a delta row, obtaining the required operator row. This changes the computation as written; the P-RW operator, projection, entropy-elbow selection, and k-means pipeline remain unchanged. An implementation change is not established.

E1.justification: Figure 8 removes the dedicated strongly connected component test cases for PolBlogs and Email-Eu. Their replacement panels use chain and core-periphery DiSBMs already evaluated elsewhere. The main dataset and clustering-task coverage remains unchanged.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparator sets in Tables 2–3 and the comparative plots are unchanged. Hermitian-SC becomes Herm-SC, while Table 1 replaces PR-SC with Sym-SC, which was already the method documented and evaluated in v2.

E3.justification: Figure 3 extends the runtime experiment from approximately 7,000 vertices to 30,000 for projected ParPIC. The main benchmark sizes, AMI/PRB metrics, projection defaults, and shared PIC evaluation controls remain unchanged; revised entropy curves do not independently establish further protocol changes.

E4.justification: The entropy-estimation validation in Figure 8 is revised: the full-graph versus strongly connected component analysis is removed, and estimator comparisons on two synthetic structures are added. The degree-heterogeneity, flow-strength, cluster-count, parameter-sensitivity, and probe-count analyses otherwise remain.

E5.justification: New Proposition 3.6 reports analytical variance and high-probability error bounds for the existing entropy estimator. This adds uncertainty quantification without establishing additional experimental runs. The 100-run means and standard deviations in Tables 2–3 and the documented 50-run analyses are retained.

E6.justification: Figure 8 replaces the post-peak declining PolBlogs and Email-Eu entropy curves with rising, saturating curves, revises other entropy estimates, and replaces two result panels. Figure 3 adds larger-graph timings. All AMI, standard-deviation, and PRB values in Tables 2–3 remain identical, limiting the result changes to supporting evaluations.

T1.justification: v3 adds Proposition 3.6 and its sampling-error derivation, an undirected consistency property and proof, and Johnson–Lindenstrauss guarantees. Definition 3.4 and Appendix E substantially correct the weighted spectral decomposition and diffusion-distance proof. The entropy proposition also addresses multiple components, but its revised proof uses mean entropy inconsistently with the summed definition.

C1.justification: The contributions remove the explicit dense-graph O(N^(3/2)) versus O(N^3) complexity claim, retaining a qualitative scalability claim. The conclusion corrects entropy maximization to entropy-elbow selection. The central claims about eigen-free directed-graph clustering and competitive accuracy remain.

C2.justification: v3 removes the warning that time selection may be ill-defined and the explanation attributing irregular PolBlogs/Email-Eu entropy to connectivity or periodicity violations. Appendix D.2 instead describes increasing entropy. Appendix D.3 adds a Johnson–Lindenstrauss rationale and guidance on logarithmic embedding dimensions for larger graphs.

D1.justification: The Software and Data statement changes from a future code-and-data release promise to a stated repository for method and experiment code. The new proof specifies uniform sampling without replacement, and Appendix D.3 suggests d=C log N with C approximately 10 for larger datasets. These disclosures do not establish changes to existing experimental settings.

R1.justification: Freksen (2021) is added to connect random projections with Johnson–Lindenstrauss theory. Table 1 corrects Simple-Herm's attribution to Laenen and Sun, already cited in v2's appendix. Other publication-year and venue updates concern retained works.

P1.justification: v3 edits grammar, standardizes method and dataset names and heading capitalization, updates affiliations and publication text, and clarifies several explanations. These are local revisions within the retained sequence of Sections 1–5 and Appendices A–E.

P2.justification: Figure 3 changes axes and legend placement; Figure 4 rearranges operator images into two rows; Figure 8 revises panels, axes, and its caption. Algorithm 1 and surrounding material are reflowed. Most table structures and other plots retain their presentation.

improvement.justification: v3 improves the diffusion-map algebra, supplies code-access information, and broadens runtime evidence. However, it replaces Figure 8's entropy behavior and removes the associated connectivity caveat without explaining the correction. Appendix E also newly mixes mean entropy in Proposition 3.5's proof with summed entropy in the method and Proposition 3.6. These unresolved issues prevent a reliable net-quality judgment.
